sq.ANSWER: Concurrent programming enables multiple computations to run in overlapping time periods—either in parallel or interleaved. It's important in modern software to efficiently use multi-core processors, reduce response time, and enhance application performance.
sq.QUESTION_DESC: Define concurrent programming and explain its importance in modern software development.

sq.ANSWER:
• Preemptive multitasking allows the OS to interrupt and switch between tasks (e.g., Windows, Linux).

  • Cooperative multitasking relies on the running task to yield control (e.g., early Mac OS).
    Java uses preemptive scheduling via the OS thread scheduler.
sq.QUESTION_DESC: Differentiate between preemptive and cooperative multitasking with examples.

lq.ANSWER:
• Use 4 threads:

    • InputThread for live response input

    • AutoSaveThread using sleep() and synchronized() to save periodically

    • MonitorThread for cheating detection (e.g., reading running processes)

    • SubmitThread triggered by timer

  • Use shared memory (variables) between threads to access responses

  • Use synchronized blocks or ReentrantLock to ensure data is not corrupted between AutoSave and Submit threads

  • Prefer multithreading over multitasking because threads are lightweight, share memory (no IPC needed), and faster to create

  • Java’s Thread Pool Executors can manage these threads efficiently

  • Possible use of TimerTask, ExecutorService, and shared data model with locking mechanism
